description: Renovate for the GitLab lane on gitlab.tomlawson.io (ai/orbit), taking over from the retired .github/dependabot.yml (#801 steps 5 and 6). Same cadence, the same grouping and the same open-request budget the Dependabot file had, so nothing about what gets watched changes with the host.

GitHub Actions is watched from here too, since the mirror flip (#801 step 5) retired .github/dependabot.yml: the 34 SHA-pinned actions and the digest-pinned Trivy image in .github/workflows/ would otherwise drift silently. GitHub still runs those workflows on the mirror as a second opinion, and publish-from-gitlab.yml is what copies the tested image to GHCR, so the pins matter. Look-ups go to github.com with GITHUB_COM_TOKEN, which the renovate job already carries.

The dependency dashboard is off (owner, 2026-09-08). It is a bot-written issue with no acceptance criteria that never reaches a done state, so it sat in a milestone that could then never report as finished, and it is stale between runs -- it listed 13 open merge requests when four were open. Turning it off changes nothing about what Renovate watches or raises; the standing assessment of the update queue lives on #882. Nothing here depends on dashboard approval.

This file is read two ways: as the repository config Renovate finds in the repository itself, and as the global config the renovate job in .gitlab-ci.yml points RENOVATE_CONFIG_FILE at. The second is what makes it work before the default branch has it -- see the job's comment.

docker-compose.description: Every docker-compose*.yml, not just the root one: the sidecars an operator actually runs are in docker-compose.yml, but the acceptance, demo, mail and local-e2e stacks pin images too, and until #771 nothing watched any of them.

customManagers.description: The pipeline pins its job images in the top-level variables block -- NODE_IMAGE, PLAYWRIGHT_IMAGE, POSTGRES_IMAGE -- and the jobs reference them as $NODE_IMAGE. The gitlabci manager reads image: and services: keys, so it sees the references and never the pins. This reads the pins. TRIVY_IMAGE is out of reach on purpose: it is pinned by digest with no tag, so there is no version to compare against, and .github/supply-chain-policy.json's scanner entry carries its review date instead.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes do not wait for Monday. GitLab CE has no dependency-alert API for Renovate to read, so osvVulnerabilityAlerts above is what supplies the advisories, from the OSV database, and this is what lets a fix for one open outside the weekly window.

packageRules.description: Every non-major update, from every manager, lands as one merge request: npm (one pnpm workspace rooted here -- pnpm-workspace.yaml lists "." and "web" -- sharing one pnpm-lock.yaml), tests/oidc/Dockerfile, the compose sidecars, the pipeline's own images (gitlabci and the custom regex manager above) and GitHub Actions. Until 2026-09-08 each manager had its own group, five merge requests a week, each queueing a full pipeline on the single runner behind the work in flight; while the project is this young, one merge request is the budget (owner, 2026-09-08). Majors stay out of the group so a breaking change is reviewed on its own.

The root Dockerfile's only FROM is the Orbit base image, whose digest comes from its own build pipeline at gitlab.tomlawson.io/ai/orbit-base-image rather than from re-resolving a registry tag here. #708 owns its freshness and scripts/sidecar-pins.mjs excludes it for exactly this reason, so Renovate must not re-pin it either.

Renovate's own image, which the gitlabci manager finds in the renovate job. 44.63.0 and 44.64.0 (both released 2026-09-04) do not start: they ship an `apk` datasource that imports `tar`, and `tar` is absent from the image's node_modules, so the container dies before it reads any configuration. Only those two are excluded, so the next working release is offered as usual. Nothing in CI runs this job, so a bump is only proven by the next scheduled run: if that run fails at start-up, revert the bump and add the version here.

The docker:*-dind service and docker:*-cli job images, which the gitlabci manager finds in .gitlab-ci.yml. Docker 29.7.0 changed how a push tracks layers across repositories (moby/moby#53081) and the daemon now sometimes skips a blob it wrongly believes the target already has, so record_image's push to registry.tomlawson.io fails with `blob unknown to registry` (moby/moby#53293, #827). 29.6.2 is unaffected and is what the pipeline holds. Only the versions seen broken are excluded -- every 29.7.x and 29.8.0 -- so whatever moby ships next (29.8.1, 29.8.4, 29.9.0) is offered in the usual weekly merge request; nothing waits for a named fix. That bump is proven by record_image: label the merge request `ci: acceptance` so the push actually runs, and if it goes red the same way, add that one version here and wait for the next.

The manual step Dependabot needed, which Renovate still needs. A sidecar pin lives in two places -- the file, and .github/supply-chain-policy.json, a bespoke schema no dependency updater parses -- so a bump lands with the two disagreeing and the drift axis of `node scripts/sidecar-pins.mjs check --offline` goes red in CI. It is not a postUpgradeTask: sync re-resolves the index digest with `docker buildx imagetools inspect`, and the renovate job runs on the shared untagged runner, which has no Docker daemon. Only orbit-build is privileged, and putting Renovate there would queue the whole pipeline behind a weekly maintenance job. So the instruction goes on the merge request, where the person who has to act on it will see it.
prBodyNotes: Before merging: run `node scripts/sidecar-pins.mjs sync` on this branch, review the diff and push it. A pin changed here may also be recorded in `.github/supply-chain-policy.json`, which this merge request does not touch, and `node scripts/sidecar-pins.mjs check --offline` fails in CI until the two agree.
